subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should builtin memory-core add durable checkpoint/resume for forced/full reindex operations, and should that behavior be automatic, implemented through reusable shadow DB state, or exposed as a memorySearch config option?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the repair changes durable memory index generation state, safe-publish semantics, and possibly public configuration, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Sponsor automatic resume
options.body: Design memory-core to resume interrupted full reindexes by default while preserving safe publish semantics and adding status/tests/docs for incomplete generations.

options.title: Use explicit opt-in config
options.body: Add checkpoint/resume behind a documented memorySearch option with upgrade proof for both default compatibility and opt-in behavior.

options.title: Defer resume and improve recovery
options.body: Keep all-or-nothing rebuilds for now and focus narrower work on retry, metadata repair, stale shadow cleanup, and clearer operator status.

recommendation.title: Sponsor automatic resume
recommendation.body: Design memory-core to resume interrupted full reindexes by default while preserving safe publish semantics and adding status/tests/docs for incomplete generations.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible history on the memory-core reindex architecture and prior issue review context.
